families.environment: Controller-to-Portainer Docker execution: resolve/create/readiness/inspect and later cleanup against a selected Docker Engine.
families.upstream: ProvisionPlan freezes installation/runtime identity, allocation and resource contract; Portainer credentials/connection revision select the endpoint; resource labels and deterministic names locate candidates.
families.observable_difference: Every runtime resolution reads Docker Engine ID and rejects a different engine; mutating requests recheck identity. Inventory treats partial/name-matching label mismatch as unknown rather than managed, and inspects candidate details before returning owned evidence. Without these gates a same-name or wrong-engine object could be acted on as this allocation. The class contract states this boundary explicitly.
families.cost: Extra Engine/info and detail GETs; endpoint/version drift or incomplete inventories block provisioning/cleanup until reconciliation. No measured latency or false rejection in this review.
families.decision: retain; Engine identity, full ownership tuple, and complete inventory protect separate facts and cannot be collapsed into labels alone.

families.environment: Prepared guest bootstrap and controller readiness; Runtime Agent authenticated API input.
families.upstream: Authenticated original request binds allocation/generation/operation and SSH key fingerprint; bootstrap requires root, supported OS/architecture/Node, prepared marker, fixed account and service configuration. Readiness authenticates SSH host key and confirms username/uid/gid/workspace write ability. Agent API requires client certificate and bearer token.
families.observable_difference: Wrong marker/identity, non-root caller, conflicting nonce, unknown SSH process or mismatched identity stays refused/unknown. Controller output is bounded (4096 combined bytes) and request body accumulation is bounded at 256 Ki JavaScript string code units (the implementation counts decoded characters, not wire bytes) so a peer cannot make readiness/request parsing unbounded. Guest SSH uses a fixed key path and key-only sshd configuration; controller does not infer access from a running service alone.
families.cost: A bootstrap/readiness mismatch blocks handoff; bounds may reject excessive diagnostic output/body. Values and validation are explicit; no credential material or real guest was used.
families.decision: retain; caller/key/guest identity and resource bounds protect distinct trust/resource boundaries. The new umask finding is a functional creation-mode defect, not a redundant gate.
